MBM prunes using travel time and distance even though the objectives are window violations and distance; the supplementary implicit LKH and OR-Tools baselines ignore windows. The O(MN^4) edge-decoding argument in Section 4.1 is implementation-dependent. Equation 24 permits only outgoing edges from the current node, leaving O(MN) candidates per step. With precomputed keys, scoring these candidates across O(N) steps and O(N) rollouts requires O(MN^3), rather than O(MN^4). An optimized direct-edge baseline is needed to substantiate the claimed architectural scaling advantage.

Practical generality remains insufficiently established. All experiments are synthetic and bi-objective; the multigraph distributions lack road-network structure and triangle inequalities. The evaluation reports mean hypervolume without confidence intervals or variation across training seeds. Small differences therefore have uncertain reliability.
